portugal_policy.title: 🇵🇹 Portugal Policy & Law
portugal_policy.content:
• **IRC SME Rate Reduction (Decreto-Lei n.º 112/2026):** Reduces the reduced corporate tax rate for the first €50,000 of taxable income for Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs), entering into force on December 1, 2026. Previously: 17%. Now: 12.5%. This increase in after-tax profit provides immediate liquidity and increases the reinvestment capacity for small Portuguese firms. Diário da República.

• **Urban Rent Ceiling Measure (Portaria n.º 401/2026):** Implements a hard cap on the annual rent update coefficient for residential leases in designated "High Pressure Zones" (Lisbon and Porto), effective immediately. Previously: Updates followed the general inflation index (CPI). Now: Capped at 2% per annum. Tenants in major cities will see significantly lower rent hikes regardless of broader inflation spikes. Diário da República.

• **2027 Minimum Wage Decree (Decreto-Lei n.º 115/2026):** Sets the national minimum wage effective January 1, 2027. Previously: €870/month. Now: €920/month. Businesses must adjust payroll budgets for the upcoming fiscal year to avoid non-compliance penalties. Portugal.gov.pt.

• **Strategic Tech Tax Incentive (Law n.º 48/2026):** Establishes a preferential personal income tax (IRS) rate for certified specialists in AI and Green Energy moving to Portugal, entering into force in 15 days. Previously: 20% under the transition NHR regime. Now: 15% for a period of 5 years. This makes Portugal more competitive in attracting high-tier global tech talent to specific strategic sectors. Assembleia da República.

Why it matters: The simultaneous reduction in SME corporate tax and the imposition of urban rent caps represent a dual effort to lower operational costs for small businesses while stabilizing living costs for the urban workforce.

us_policy.title: 🇺🇸 United States Policy
us_policy.content:
• **Executive and Legislative Actions:** No executive orders were signed by the President and no bills were enacted into law by Congress between November 10 and November 12, 2026. Previously: Routine legislative activity. Now: Zero new binding laws or orders enacted. This indicates no new presidential or congressional mandates affecting market operations. White House / Congress.gov.

• **Regulatory Agency Final Rules:** No final rules with significant market impact were published in the Federal Register by the SEC, Fed, FTC, or DOJ from November 10 to November 12, 2026. Previously: Periodic regulatory issuance. Now: No new finalized mandates or prohibited actions. This removes immediate regulatory risk for US equity holdings in these sectors. Federal Register.

• **Trade and Sanctions Actions:** No new sanctions designations or trade actions were issued by the Department of Treasury or Department of Commerce between November 10 and November 12, 2026. Previously: Regular sanctions updates. Now: No new trade restrictions or entity listings. This maintains the current status quo for international trade and US-based exporters. Federal Register.

Why it matters: The US policy pipeline is quiet, providing a period of regulatory stability for long-term investors this week.
